I found a wallet in a shopping cart at Walmart last Tuesday. Brown leather. Worn soft at the edges. Tucked under one of those reusable bags someone had left behind.

I almost didn't see it. I was returning my cart because that's what I do — I'm the person who walks it back to the corral instead of leaving it in the middle of the parking lot like an animal. My husband makes fun of me for it. Says I'm the last honest person in America. I tell him somebody has to be.

The wallet was light. No credit cards. No debit card. Just a driver's license and $400 in cash. Twenty-dollar bills, folded tight,

Took his 40mg Lipitor every morning at 7 sharp.

He did everything the doctor told him.
